pre: The named people are the attached Characters, with their own faces and clothes.
end: Muted colour: stone grey, black and navy, with small touches of red and blue the only strong colour. Unretouched, natural skin texture, visible 35mm film grain. Nobody looks at the camera. 16:9. Thanks.
riotEnd: Dusk, with a deep cold blue sky. Colour: stone grey and near-black, with the hot pink-red of flare light and one cold blue the only strong colours. Hand-held documentary photography: the frame is tilted well off level, there is slight motion blur on moving hands and flags, the highlights of the flare are blown out, and the film grain is heavy. Unretouched. Nobody looks at the camera. 16:9. Thanks.
camEnd: Flat harsh on-camera light that falls off to black a few feet behind them, red-eye in one pair of eyes, slight motion blur, video noise in the shadows, washed-out colour. Unretouched, natural skin texture, shiny foreheads. 16:9. Thanks.

shots.body: Match the attached photograph br5-riot-look for look only: the same dusk, the same wet cobbles, the same hot pink-red flare light and smoke, the same low tilted hand-held camera. Do not copy its people or its framing. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 20mm lens lying on the cobbles inside a crowd, looking steeply up. A red hand flare burns on the cobbles in the near left foreground, out of focus, and its smoke drifts up across the lower third of the frame. The leg of a steel crowd barrier crosses the near right foreground. Above, two hand-painted cardboard placards on wooden sticks are held up by gloved hands, one on each side of the barrier, against the sky: the left placard has a red painted border and the right placard has a blue painted border. Each placard reads, in the same uneven black hand-painted capitals, "WE CAN'T AFFORD TO LIVE HERE". The bottom edge of each placard is hidden behind the hoods and woolly hats of the people holding them, seen from below and behind. The cardboard is rain-spotted and one corner is bent. Far behind, small, are the dark stone columns of a bank with two lit windows. One light source only, no fill: the flare on the ground, lighting the cardboard and the undersides of chins from below. The faces under the hoods are in shadow.

Match the attached photograph br5-riot-look for look only: the same dusk, the same wet cobbles, the same hot pink-red flare light and smoke, the same low tilted hand-held camera. Do not copy its people or its framing. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with an 18mm lens lying on the wet cobbles in an empty strip of road between two lines of steel crowd barriers, looking up. A dense crowd in winter coats is packed behind each barrier. On the left, rising above his crowd, nearer and larger, Mr Blue stands on an upturned plastic crate shouting into a megaphone and pointing across the frame to the right. On the right, further off and smaller, Mr Red stands on his own crate above his crowd, shouting into his own megaphone and pointing back to the left. Their pointing arms cross against the sky. Plain blue cloth flags rise from the crowd on the left and plain red cloth flags from the crowd on the right. A red hand flare burns on the cobbles in the near foreground, out of focus, with a trampled paper cup beside it, and its smoke drifts across the bottom of the frame. Far behind, between the two men, are the stone columns of a bank with lit windows. One light source only, no fill: the flare on the ground, lighting the two men from below. Their eye sockets are dark.

Match the attached photograph br5-riot-look for look only: the same dusk, the same wet cobbles, the same hot pink-red flare light and smoke, the same low tilted hand-held camera. Do not copy its people or its framing. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 16mm lens lying on the cobbles at the foot of a bank, looking steeply up its front. The stone columns climb away to a heavy stone frieze, and carved across the frieze in deep Roman capitals is one word: "BANK". There is no other lettering anywhere. In the near foreground, out of focus, a trampled cardboard placard lies face down in a puddle with a boot print across it, beside a spent flare. The tips of plain red cloth flags cut into the bottom left corner and the tips of plain blue cloth flags into the bottom right corner. Pink smoke drifts across the lower half of the columns. Three tall windows between the columns are lit warm from inside. One light source only, no fill: a flare burning out of frame at the bottom left, raking up the stone. The top of the building goes dark against the sky.

Match the attached photograph br5-riot-look for look only: the same dusk, the same wet cobbles, the same hot pink-red flare light and smoke, the same low tilted hand-held camera. Do not copy its people or its framing. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 20mm lens lying on the cobbles in an empty strip of road between two lines of steel crowd barriers, looking up along it. The out-of-focus back of a police officer's yellow high-visibility jacket fills the near right third of the frame, one gloved hand on a barrier. Walking up the strip toward the camera, off-centre to the left, The Ex comes on unhurried in a long dark overcoat, hands in his pockets, looking ahead past the lens. A step behind his shoulder The Fixer follows, chewing. Behind them two men in black suits, small and soft, haul a hand pallet truck stacked with shrink-wrapped blocks of paper. Behind each barrier a crowd stands with its backs turned to the strip, facing outward, under plain red cloth flags on the left and plain blue cloth flags on the right. One light source only, no fill: a red hand flare held up in the crowd on the left, behind the men, rim-lighting their shoulders and the smoke. Their faces are mostly in shadow.

A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 28mm lens, locked off and perfectly still, low at the height of a table top at the back of a dark upstairs sitting room. A man in a black suit stands at a tall sash window with his back to the camera, small in the frame and well off-centre to the right, a black silhouette. One arm hangs at his side and the hand holds a television remote control. Heavy dark red velvet curtains hang from the ceiling to the floor on both sides of the window. In the near left foreground, out of focus, a small table lamp with a fringed shade is switched on, very dim, beside a black dial telephone on a dark wooden table. The floorboards are bare and there is a wide empty stretch of floor between the camera and the man. Through the glass no street can be seen, only slow smoke lit hot pink-red from below and, further off, a cold blue glow. The only light is that glow through the window, which throws the man's long shadow back across the floorboards toward the camera, and the dim amber lamp. The ceiling and the corners of the room are black.

A frame from a cheap hand-held camcorder with its own small light switched on, too close and tilted. A wood-panelled private bar in a large house, late at night. Mr Blue and Mr Red stand with their drinking arms linked at the elbow, each tipping a full pint of lager down his throat with his eyes shut, beer running down their chins onto their white shirts, ties pulled loose, jackets off. Behind them and between them The Governor sits bolt upright on a bar stool in his buttoned jacket holding a very small glass of sherry, watching them with no expression. A row of empty shot glasses and a chewed lemon wedge on the edge of the bar cut into the near foreground, out of focus. Behind them is dark wood panelling and nothing else. The only light is the camcorder's own lamp.

A frame from a cheap hand-held camcorder with its own small light switched on, too close and tilted. The camera is held against the wall right beside a pub dartboard, looking back along the throw. The edge of the dartboard and three darts stuck in the wood panelling well wide of it cut into the near right foreground, out of focus. At the throwing line The Accountant stands side-on with one eye screwed shut and the tip of his tongue between his teeth, a dart raised beside his ear, shirt sleeves rolled, tie over his shoulder, swaying. Behind him The Fixer crouches behind an armchair with a sausage roll in his mouth and one arm over his head. A fourth dart is stuck in a framed oil painting of a horse on the far wall. The only light is the camcorder's own lamp.

A frame from a cheap hand-held camcorder with its own small light switched on, too close and tilted. The camera rests on the green cloth of a pool table at the height of the balls. The white ball and the black ball sit close to the lens at the left, out of focus. Mr Turquoise lies on his stomach right across the table in his shirt and turquoise tie, one shoe missing, lining up a shot with the cue held behind his back, grinning with his eyes half shut. A knocked-over pint glass lies beside him and a dark stain of lager spreads into the cloth. Behind the table The Donor sits in a leather armchair with his face in one hand. Behind them is dark wood panelling and nothing else. The only light is the camcorder's own lamp.

A frame from a cheap hand-held camcorder with its own small light switched on, too close and tilted. Inside a marquee on a lawn at night. The Fixer kneels on the grass bent double over a silver champagne ice bucket that he hugs with both arms, his face hidden down inside it, his jacket ridden up his back and his tie hanging in the bucket. Right beside him The Proprietor sits in a folding chair with his walking stick between his knees, staring straight ahead, not looking at him. A man's hand in a black sleeve comes in from the right edge and pats The Fixer on the back while holding a champagne flute. A chocolate fountain cuts into the near left foreground, out of focus. Behind them is the pale lining of the marquee and nothing else. The only light is the camcorder's own lamp.

A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with an 85mm lens at the edge of a trestle table in a lock-up garage, close, from behind two newspapers. Two open newspapers are held up close to the lens, one in each of his hands, and we see only their outer sides from behind: soft, out-of-focus grey newsprint with blurred columns of tiny text, filling the left third and the right third of the frame. There is no masthead, no title, no logo, no headline and no photograph on them, and not one word can be read. In the gap between them, sharp, Mr Red looks from one newspaper to the other with his mouth slightly open, puzzled. On the table beside his elbow an open laptop shows only The Platform's face on a video call, lit by his own screen, looking bored, with no writing on the screen. A mug of cold tea with the bag still in it stands by the laptop. Behind them is a bare breeze-block wall and nothing else. One light source only, no fill: one bare bulb hanging above the table. The far side of Mr Red's face falls into deep shadow.
shots.note: second try: the first put a real newspaper masthead on one of the papers, facing the camera

shots.body: A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 24mm lens lying on the marble floor of a bank corridor, looking up, the frame tilted well off level. Three men stand some way off, seen full length. At the left Mr Blue and at the right Mr Red face each other in profile, each holding a small black pistol out at arm's length toward the other, both shouting. Between them and a little further back The Presenter stands square with his arms spread wide, a pistol in each hand, one aimed at each of the other two, with a calm professional smile. A dropped cardboard carnival mask and a paper banknote band lie on the floor in the near foreground, out of focus. One light source only, no fill: one red alarm lamp turning on the wall behind them. It rim-lights their shoulders and the pistols in hard red, throws three long shadows up the corridor toward the camera, and leaves their faces mostly dark. The far end of the corridor is black.

A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 35mm lens at knee height on a wet pavement at night in heavy rain, looking up and across a narrow road, the frame not quite level. Denise stands in the near right foreground with her back three-quarters to the camera, in her work tabard under an open anorak, her hair soaked flat, a carrier bag hanging from one hand, completely still, looking across the road. Across the road, sharp, is a small café with its steel shutter down and a plain unlettered fascia, and above it the brick wall of a flat with one dark sash window and a pot plant on the sill inside. Fixed flat to the brick beside that window is an estate agent's board, plain red, with one word on it in very large bold white capital letters: "SOLD". There is no other writing anywhere. One light source only, no fill: one orange street lamp above the café, with the rain falling through its light. The wet road reflects the lamp and the red board. She is a dark shape with an orange rim. Everything else is black.

A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with an 85mm lens held low at the height of her collar, looking up at Denise's face from below and slightly to one side, at night in heavy rain. Her head and shoulders fill the lower two thirds of the frame, off-centre to the left. She looks straight ahead, level, past the lens, her mouth shut, her hair soaked flat to her forehead, rain running down her cheeks and dripping from her chin and the collar of her anorak. Above and behind her is black sky with streaks of rain caught in the light, and the dark out-of-focus top of a lamp post at the right edge. One light source only, no fill: one orange street lamp behind her and to the right, rim-lighting her wet hair and one cheek. The other side of her face is in deep shadow with one small glint in the eye.

later.body: The attached photograph br5-cafe shows a café with a flat above it at night. Show the same café, the same brick wall, the same sash window and the same pot plant on a grey wet morning. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 35mm lens at knee height on the pavement across the road, looking up, the frame not quite level. In the near left foreground, out of focus, a man's hand in a black suit sleeve with a white cuff holds up a bunch of house keys on a ring, each key with a paper tag, dangling from one finger. Across the road, sharp, the café's steel shutter is half up, its window is steamed from inside and one strip light is on. On the brick beside the flat's window is an estate agent's board, plain red, with two words in very large bold white capital letters: "FOR SALE". There is no other writing anywhere. A wet road, a parked bicycle and bin bags by the door. One light source only, no fill: flat grey overcast daylight from above. The flat's window is dark.

endLynch: Colour: black, deep red and one small amber point. Deep shadows with no detail in them, soft halation around the window glow, visible 35mm film grain. Unretouched. 16:9. Thanks.
endLens: Muted colour: stone grey, black and navy, with small touches of red and blue the only strong colour. Unretouched, natural skin texture, visible 35mm film grain. 16:9. Thanks.
